item.title: Africa faces ‘complex’ Ebola outbreak after virus spread to Nigeria – WHO
item.description: The World Health Organization’s Africa chief warned on Thursday that the continent now faced a “complex” Ebola outbreak after the virus crossed from east Africa to Nigeria, which has reported the first case in the west of the continent. “We are facing a more complex outbreak landscape. Nigeria has confirmed an imported case of Ebola virus disease,” Mohamed Janabi, the regional director for WHO in Africa, told an online media briefing. Nigeria on Tuesday announced an imported case of the Bundibugyo strain behind a major DR Congo outbreak, in a woman, a diplomat who had a history of travel to Uganda. The continent’s most populous nation is the fourth African country affected by the outbreak, which this week came to span the continent, with Kenya in the east reporting nine cases since October 6. The case reignited memories of a widespread outbreak in 2014 that struck several countries in the region and killed more than 11,000 people across west Africa between late 2013 and 2016. Nigeria’s experience in successfully containing the Ebola outbreak in 2014 raised confidence that the country can respond effectively to new public health threats. The DRC’s Ebola epidemic has become the deadliest in the country’s history, killing 4,381 people out of more than 9,000 confirmed cases since mid-May, according to the health authorities. item.title: US Embassy issues health alert to Americans in Nigeria amid Bundibugyo Ebola case
item.description: The United States Embassy in Abuja has issued a health alert following Nigeria’s report of a case of Bundibugyo virus disease, a form of Ebola, on October 20, 2026. In the alert published on October 21, the US Mission Nigeria said health officials were conducting contact tracing after the case was reported. According to the alert, the Nigerian Ministry of Health said the affected individual had travelled by air from Uganda. The embassy described Ebola as a serious health concern, stating that “Ebola is a rare, severe, and often fatal hemorrhagic fever illness.” The US Embassy urged travelers to consult health guidance from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and take precautions against possible exposure to the virus. It advised people to visit the CDC’s Ebola information page and its travel health page for Nigeria for relevant information. The embassy also advised people who may be at risk of Ebola to alert their healthcare providers if they experience symptoms consistent with the disease, so they can receive guidance before presenting for medical care. Travellers were further advised to continue taking malaria preventive medication as recommended by their doctors, noting that malaria symptoms can resemble those of Ebola and trigger avoidable health scares. The alert also urged people returning from areas experiencing an Ebola outbreak to monitor their health for 21 days after travel. The US Embassy advised travellers to consult the US Department of State’s Nigeria country page for general health information. It also directed them to the embassy’s list of medical providers and encouraged them to contact their travel insurance providers to understand available medical evacuation options if they become ill while overseas. item.title: FCT Police intercept SUV with concealed presidency number plate
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi FCT Police Command operatives have intercepted a Lexus LX570 SUV with a concealed number plate in Maitama District of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). According to the Police, officers intercepted the SUV on 20th October 2026, at about 8 pm, and promptly arrested the occupant for investigation and subsequent prosecution. Spokesperson of the command, SP Josephine Adeh, said, “Preliminary investigations revealed that the concealed number plate bore the inscription ‘PRESIDENCY’ and registration number 10B218 FG. “Following the suspect’s claim of being the legitimate holder of the number plate, further investigations revealed that the plate’s registration documents were forged and that the suspect was impersonating a Permanent Secretary attached to the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation. “Investigations are ongoing, and the suspect will be charged to court upon their conclusion. “The FCT Police Command urges residents to remain law-abiding, cooperate with police operations, and promptly report suspicious persons or activities to the nearest Police Station or through the Command’s emergency numbers: 08032003913, 08061581938.” The post FCT Police intercept SUV with concealed presidency number plate appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Foreign national beaten to death by mob in South Africa
item.description: A mob of about 50 people beat a foreign national to death Thursday in South Africa’s port city of Durban, a flashpoint for anti-migrant sentiment, police said. Durban has been a focus of months of protests against foreign nationals, with looting and violence erupting after an anti-migrant march in the city two weeks ago. Thursday’s attack in the city centre was on the sidelines of a march, police said, without being able to say what the demonstration was about. Two men from the group approached another man, aged in his late 30s or early 40s, who was on the side of the road, police said. “It is further alleged that the victim was then assaulted by a group of about 50 people and he was declared dead at the scene,” a police statement said. The nationality of the man and the motive for the attack was unknown. Drivers with e-hailing services marched in the same area on Wednesday in a demonstration involving the March and March movement, which has mobilised protests against illegal migrants across the country for months. Two weeks ago, soldiers were deployed to central Durban as police battled to control two days of rioting and looting in unrest targeted at foreign nationals. Fourteen vehicles were set alight and businesses were looted or torched. The violence echoed weeks of protests that led tens of thousands of nationals from other African nations to flee earlier this year. item.title: Why Africa is without vaccine for latest Ebola strain — Africa CDC
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The Director-General of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, Dr Jean Kaseya, has blamed a lack of international interest for the absence of an approved vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, saying the situation might have been different if the outbreak were affecting Western countries. Kaseya made the remarks on Thursday during an interview on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief, where he called for greater African investment in vaccine research and manufacturing. He said, “I can tell you, if this outbreak was in Western countries, vaccine will already be available. Why this vaccine today is not available? Because some of our partners decided to consider this issue as an African issue, they were not interested.” The Africa CDC chief, however, said the agency was taking steps to address the gap, including supporting clinical trials of vaccine candidates. He disclosed that an African manufacturer in Egypt was conducting clinical trials of a potential vaccine targeting the Bundibugyo strain. Kaseya also said the agency was working with the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda to explore clinical trials and compassionate use of Ervebo, a vaccine developed for the Zaire strain of Ebola. He stressed that the continent had the expertise and capacity to advance vaccine development, adding that Africa should not continue to depend solely on external partners during public health emergencies. “We don’t want to see Africa left behind. We have the knowledge, we have people with intelligence, we have capacity to manufacture vaccines, and we need to move on,” he said. Kaseya also called for greater domestic funding and improved coordination among African countries and international partners. He said 28 African countries had contributed funding to support the response to the current outbreak. The Bundibugyo strain has no licensed vaccine or approved specific treatment. The outbreak, declared in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in May 2026, has caused more than 9,000 confirmed cases and 4,381 deaths, according to Congolese health authorities The disease has also been detected in other countries, with the Kenyan Health Ministry reporting a ninth case in the country on Tuesday, prompting concerns over cross-border transmission. Nigeria also confirmed its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola in the Federal Capital Territory on October 20. The patient, a woman with a recent travel history to Uganda, is receiving medical care, while health authorities have identified 44 contacts for monitoring. item.title: Beyond Price Predictions: Exploring Binarium’s Trading Tools and Features
item.description: Ask a beginner what trading is, and the answer is usually “guessing whether a price will go up or down.” But the click that opens a trade is the shortest part of the process. What shapes your results is everything around it: how you practise, how you read the market, where your ideas come from and how you manage risk. That is why a platform’s tools matter more than its buttons. Binarium is an online trading platform that has been operating since 2012. It is available in a browser and as an Android or iOS app, and offers up to 129 assets depending on the account type. The platform supports naira accounts and local payment methods for Nigerian users. Around the trade ticket sits a full set of learning and analysis tools: a demo account, a TradingView chart, an economic calendar, a Trading Room with ideas from experienced traders. This guide explains what each tool does, why it is useful and where its limits are. 1. The Binarium demo account: practise with a purpose New users receive a demo account with ₦10,000,000 in virtual funds. You can switch between demo and real accounts at any time by clicking your balance in the terminal. Demo funds cannot be withdrawn. You can explore the platform’s features through a Binarium demo account before considering real-money trading. Alt: Binarium trading platform A trade is simple in structure: choose an asset, an expiry time and an amount, then decide whether the price will be higher or lower at expiry. If the asset shows a 90% payout and you stake ₦10,000, a correct prediction returns your stake plus ₦9,000, while a wrong one costs the full ₦10,000. Payouts vary by asset. Instead of clicking around, give the demo a job: Test one idea repeatedly, such as one indicator on one timeframe, and see how it behaves over many trades. Review the History section afterwards and look for patterns in your own decisions. Notice how you react after a loss. That is the habit worth fixing before real money is involved. A line chart shows the overall direction, while candlesticks add the open, high, low and close of each period. Alt: candle size Binarium website The standard chart includes popular indicators and drawing tools: SMA (simple moving average) smooths price data so the underlying trend is easier to see. Bollinger Bands show how stretched the price is compared with its recent range. Drawing tools such as segments and curves let you mark support, resistance and channels directly on the chart. And the trader sentiment scale shows what share of current trades on an asset expect the price to rise and what share expects it to fall. It reflects what the crowd is doing, not what the market will do. The economic calendar: knowing when the market may move The Economic Calendar section lists scheduled events with filters for yesterday, today, tomorrow and the week. Each entry shows how long is left until the event, the country, the event name and a strength indicator of one to three triangles. The more triangles, the bigger the event’s expected impact on the market. A routine government bond auction carries one, while a major employment report typically carries three. Treat every card as a hypothesis to check: look at the chart, decide your own stake, and test the approach on a demo account first. No trader’s call is guaranteed, including a professional’s. Nigerian users can open an account in naira or in US dollars. You choose the currency at registration, and it cannot be changed later. Minimum amounts. The minimum deposit is ₦5,000. The minimum trade is around ₦1,000. Minimums can vary by payment system, so check the Cashier. Payment methods. The Cashier for Nigeria includes bank transfer, Visa cards and the local wallets OPay and PalmPay. Crypto options include Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT and USDC, as well as Binance Pay and Bybit Pay. Methods can change, so check the Cashier after registering. NFX mode. Besides the standard mode, where each asset shows its own payout percentage, Binarium offers NFX mode, where the payout is calculated for every trade separately. It depends on factors such as the number of active traders and the volatility of the asset. A variable payout does not change the risk: a wrong prediction still costs the full stake. Fees and withdrawals. Binarium states that it covers payment-system fees on deposits and withdrawals, subject to its terms. Identity verification is required before you withdraw. item.title: France reports first human Shamonda virus case, says no health risk
item.description: French health authorities said Thursday that the Shamonda virus, which usually affects livestock, had been detected in a human for the first time, in a severely immunocompromised patient who died earlier this month. There was “no health risk to the general public identified at this time”, the health and agriculture ministries said in a joint statement. It added that the human infection appeared to be “an exceptional case involving a severely immunocompromised patient” hospitalised for a serious medical condition. “Despite circulating in Africa and Asia for several decades, the Shamonda virus has never previously been detected in humans,” the ministries said. The virus, which belongs to the Orthobunyavirus group and is typically transmitted to animals by small biting insects, was first detected in Europe this summer, they said. At this stage in the investigation, the patient was believed to have contracted the virus through the bite of a midge in eastern France, where the virus was circulating in animals during the spring and summer, the ministries said. “The neurological complications observed in the immunocompromised patient prior to his death are very likely linked to infection with the Shamonda virus,” they added, citing preliminary findings. But “clinical, biological and epidemiological investigations are still ongoing”, they said. – In 14 European countries – The virus was first detected in Nigeria in the mid-1960s and has since been reported in cattle in several parts of Africa and in Japan. The virus was detected in Europe for the first time at the end of July, including on cattle farms in France. It has now been detected in 14 western European countries, according to an epidemiological bulletin from France’s national research institute monitoring animal health. Cattle are considered its main animal hosts, although sporadic infections in smaller livestock and horses have also been identified in France this summer. In cattle, the main symptoms are acute diarrhoea, fever, lethargy and a drop in milk production. An investigation is ongoing, and both the World Health Organization and the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control have been notified. item.title: Who won Lagos in 2023?
item.description: By Sekinat Osundiji Peter Obi of the Labour Party (LP) defeated Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Lagos State in the February 25, 2023, presidential election, overturning expectations in a state long regarded as Tinubu’s political stronghold. Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) received 8,442 votes. Obi won Lagos by 9,848 votes, making the result one of the major surprises of the 2023 presidential election. Tinubu, who governed Lagos from 1999 to 2007, had maintained significant political influence in the state through his party and political network. However, the result showed that his longstanding connection to Lagos did not guarantee victory at the polls. item.title: French city of Lyon bans ‘all protests’ on Saturday
item.description: Officials have banned “all protests” in France’s third-biggest city of Lyon on Saturday, ahead of nationwide demonstrations that day following rallies last weekend that descended into widespread street violence. The prefecture for the Rhone region said on Thursday in a statement to media that, “given the events of October 17, the prefect has decided to ban by decree all protests in the city of Lyon this Saturday, October 24”. Lyon, like Paris and other French cities, suffered clashes and looting when masked youths took to city centre streets on the sidelines of mass rallies protesting high inflation. The mayor of Lyon, Gregory Doucet, has said that his city experienced hours of “chaos” during the riots, with between 150 and 200 shops looted and a tourist office torched. Police arrested some 200 people. The organisers of the rallies, the Yellow Vest movement and unions, have called for another round of nationwide demonstrations over the cost of living on Saturday, and a general strike and demonstrations on November 5. French officials who found themselves unable to contain last weekend’s violence this week ordered three nights of curfews in parts of Paris, Lyon and some other cities to protect shopping districts. item.title: Court Resumes Trial Of Suspects Linked To Abduction Of NYSC Members, Others In Imo
item.description: Court is set to resume the trial of suspects linked to the abduction of 20 members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) and others in Imo State. The suspects were apprehended in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, and Abia State during intelligence-led operations conducted between October 10 and 14 by the Department of State Services (DSS), in collaboration with the military, police, and other security operatives. Three other suspects reportedly escaped with gunshot wounds, prompting a manhunt for the fleeing members of the gang. The prospective corps members were abducted along the Owerri-Onitsha Expressway in Imo State on October 1, 2026, while they were travelling from Ibadan, Oyo State, to their assigned NYSC orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states. The gunmen attacked two buses conveying the prospective corps members and other passengers near Umunoha in the Mbaitoli Local Government Area of Imo State. The victims were rescued on October 7 during a joint security operation at Amakohia-Ubi Village in Owerri West Local Government Area of the state. They were subsequently taken to the DSS hospital in Owerri for medical attention and necessary checks. During the search-and-rescue operation, the police had said their operatives located the kidnappers’ camp through drone surveillance but could not immediately advance because the location was reportedly planted with improvised explosive devices (IEDs). Security agencies later intensified efforts to reach the victims and secure their release. item.title: Ebola: Medical laboratory scientists urge virtual campaigns ahead of 2027 elections
item.description: The Association of Medical Laboratory Scientists of Nigeria (AMLSN), Kaduna State Branch, has advised political parties to campaign virtually to minimise physical contact amid the Ebola outbreak. Mr Turman Benjamin, Chairman of the association in Kaduna gave the advice on Thursday in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in Kaduna. Benjamin recommended social media, text messages, telephone calls and virtual meeting platforms such as Zoom and Google Meet as alternatives to physical political rallies. He said the approach would reduce unnecessary contact and help minimise potential exposure while health authorities worked to contain the outbreak. Benjamin urged the Kaduna State Government to intensify public awareness, trace any contacts linked to the confirmed case and ensure adequate protective equipment for healthcare workers. He advised residents to avoid unnecessary physical contact, including handshakes and hugs, and observe appropriate hygiene measures. The medical laboratory scientist said Ebola could be transmitted through direct contact with the blood and other bodily fluids of infected persons. He also urged the public to avoid handling the bodies of suspected or confirmed Ebola victims without appropriate training and protective equipment. Benjamin said only trained and properly equipped personnel should handle such bodies to reduce the risk of infection during burial preparations. He called on the government to provide hospitals with adequate personal protective equipment, including gloves and other appropriate protective gear. According to him, laboratory testing is essential to confirm Ebola because its early symptoms can resemble those of other illnesses, including malaria and typhoid fever. Benjamin further advised the public to exercise caution when handling or consuming wild animals that could carry infectious diseases. He urged the media to intensify public education on Ebola transmission, prevention and the importance of seeking prompt medical attention when symptoms develop. The chairman also called for vigilance among healthcare workers and members of the public, stressing the importance of early detection and effective infection prevention measures. The NAN reports that the Federal Government has confirmed one case of Ebola disease in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, with 44 close contacts identified for monitoring to prevent further transmission. The patient, a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda, was admitted to a private hospital in the FCT, where she received treatment for several days before the diagnosis was confirmed. The woman has since been placed in isolation and is receiving medical care, while health authorities have commenced contact tracing to identify and monitor people who may have been exposed to the virus.( NAN ) The post Ebola: Medical laboratory scientists urge virtual campaigns ahead of 2027 elections appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Troops rescue four kidnapped victims in Zamfara, Kebbi
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Sector 2, Operation Fansan Yamma, have rescued four kidnapped victims during separate intelligence-led operations in Zamfara and Kebbi states as the military intensifies efforts to combat terrorism and kidnapping across the North West. According to the Army, the victims were rescued on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, in Maru Local Government Area of Zamfara State and between Bena and Sawade in Kebbi State. “In Zamfara, troops rescued Mansur Shehu, 25, and Kadijat Haruna, 49, following a response to a reported terrorist incident on farmland across a river in Binoni Marafa, Maru LGA. “In Kebbi, troops conducted a search-and-rescue operation after receiving reports of suspected terrorists moving with kidnapped victims from Dupindu Village, Kanya District, Danko-Wasagu LGA. “The operation secured the freedom of Jimoh Su-Arege, 35, and Kalahe Danjuma, 41, who were subsequently handed over to the Seriki of Dipindu. “The military said troops have continued to intensify patrols and surveillance across affected communities to strengthen security, dominate operational areas and deny criminal elements freedom of action. “The successful operations highlight Operation Fansan Yamma’s sustained efforts to rescue abducted persons, disrupt terrorist activities and restore peace across Zamfara and Kebbi states,” the military said. item.description: By James Ogunnaike Abeokuta The Ogun State government has ordered the closure of some schools in Ijebu-Ode, Ago-Iwoye and Ijebu-Igbo following the hospitalisation of more than 100 pupils on Wednesday after suspected exposure to an offensive gaseous substance. Among the schools worst affected were Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School, Anglican Girls Grammar School, Ijebu-Ode, Itamerin Comprehensive High School and some schools in Ago-Iwoye. item.title: Iran’s Guards threaten to hit US bases in retaliation for Hormuz escorts
item.description: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards on Thursday threatened to strike American bases across the Middle East if the US military continues to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz. “The US military must know that if this trend continues, the conflict will extend to its bases in the region,” the Guards, the ideological arm of Iran’s military, said in a statement on their Sepah News website. “This is a serious warning,” they added. Iran claims control over Hormuz, a strategic shipping route through which one-fifth of the world’s oil supplies passed before war broke out in February. It regularly attacks ships that attempt to navigate the strait without its authorisation. But the US military has been escorting vessels through the waterway in increasing numbers, with Iran responding by stepping up attacks. Four ships were hit in the area overnight as they attempted to pass through the wider Gulf, Iranian forces said on Thursday. Washington has also been maintaining a naval blockade on Iranian ports in an attempt to squeeze the country’s economy, while negotiations to end the conflict are deadlocked. Hormuz, bordered to the north by Iran and to the south by Oman, is only about 30 kilometres (19 miles) wide at its narrowest point and is a critical route for ships carrying oil and gas from energy-rich Gulf countries. item.title: Sowore claps back after Senator Ajibola called him ‘skit maker’
item.description: The presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), Omoyele Sowore, has hit back at the National Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Ajibola Basiru, after the senator described him as a “skit maker” and “comedian”. Sowore, in a statement posted on X, recalled his longstanding relationship with Basiru, saying they fought against military dictatorship together in the 1990s. He also accused the APC chieftain of abandoning the democratic ideals they once defended because of the privileges of his current political position. The exchange followed Basiru’s appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday, where he described Sowore as a skit maker. Responding, Sowore shared a photograph of himself with Basiru taken in 1998, when he led the Congress of Progressive Youths (COPY), a pro-democracy group. “I watched an interview on Politics Today on Channels Television, anchored by Seun Okinbaloye, in which the APC National Secretary, Ajibola Basiru, called me a ‘skit maker’ and ‘comedian’,” he wrote. Sowore said he received Basiru at the University of Lagos after the latter was expelled from the University of Ilorin in 1992 over student activism. He said he and other activists, including Kunle Adegoke, popularly known as K-Rad, helped Basiru secure an opportunity to return to the university and study law. “Both eventually graduated with flying colours and went on to accomplish great things,” Sowore said, adding that their shared history made Basiru’s remarks particularly disappointing. He argued that the struggle for democracy and human dignity should not be dismissed as entertainment, insisting that his activism remained consistent with the ideals they defended during military rule. “The struggle for justice, democracy, freedom and the preservation of human dignity is neither skit-making nor comedy,” he said. Sowore also faulted Basiru’s argument that opposition candidates should be ashamed of losing to President Bola Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election, which he described as deeply flawed. He maintained that political appointments were temporary and predicted that Tinubu’s administration, like previous military regimes, would eventually leave office. “Political appointments are temporary. Tinubu’s regime will come and go, just like the military regimes we confronted in our youth,” he said. Sowore concluded by accusing Basiru of turning against the ideals he once championed. “What is truly comical is watching yesterday’s beneficiaries of resistance become today’s defenders of the very oppression they once fought against,” he wrote. item.title: Ekiti Assembly passes State Police Bill
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela The Ekiti State House of Assembly has passed the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, seeking to provide for the establishment of State Police Services in Nigeria. The bill scaled second and third readings during plenary on Tuesday, with all 21 members present voting in support, signalling the Assembly’s endorsement of decentralised policing. Following its passage, the Speaker, Rt. Hon. Adeoye Stephen Aribasoye, directed the Clerk of the House to transmit the document to the National Assembly alongside observations made by the state legislature. Speaking on the bill, Aribasoye said state police had remained at the forefront of national discourse for over two decades, noting that the Ekiti Assembly had a historic opportunity to take a position. He stressed the need for effective and responsive security, saying Nigeria’s policing challenges required practical solutions. “Nigerians had repeatedly expressed concerns over delayed responses to distress calls, limitations in operational reach and the distance between law enforcement agencies and the communities they were meant to protect,” he said. The Speaker added that inadequate and poorly coordinated local policing in some areas had contributed to insecurity, threatening livelihoods, disrupting education, undermining business confidence and eroding public trust. He said a properly structured State Police system could strengthen accountability by bringing policing leadership and oversight closer to the people and their elected representatives, subject to constitutional safeguards. According to him, the country could not afford unnecessary delays in addressing security challenges, describing State Police as “a long-overdue practical necessity rather than a mere theoretical preference.” In its report, the Committee of the Whole House recommended concurrence to the bill, subject to an amendment to Section 317A(5). The committee said it considered the bill clause by clause and deliberated on the proposed constitutional framework for the establishment and operation of State Police Services. It proposed the insertion of the words “an Act of the National Assembly or a Law of the State House of Assembly, as applicable” after the words “this Constitution” in the newly inserted Section 317A(5). The observation, the committee noted, is intended to expressly recognise the legislative authority of the National Assembly and State Houses of Assembly, within their respective constitutional jurisdictions, in authorising relevant security arrangements. item.title: Libya recovers Swiss, Austrian women kidnapped since 2025 in Niger
item.description: Two women — one Swiss and the other Austrian — were released from more than a year of captivity in Niger and arrived in Libya’s eastern city of Benghazi, Libyan media outlets reported on Thursday. The two women — Swiss national Eva Gretzmacher, 76, and Austrian Claudia Abbt, 69 — were abducted in Niger in 2025. In a video released by Libya’s eastern-based al-Masar TV, the women appeared emaciated and thanked the country’s eastern-based military commander Khalifa Haftar and his son, Saddam, for their release. Al-Masar said “two hostages, an Austrian and a Swiss national, have been freed after being held captive in Niger for a year and a half”. “My name is Eva Gretzmacher, I am 76, and I thank from the bottom of my heart Marshal Haftar and his son, Saddam, who released us,” one of the woman said in French. “I had been held hostage for a year and nine months,” she said. Abbt said she was “happy to be free”, also thanking Haftar. Online website Libyan News Observatory also reported their release. Libya has struggled to recover from the chaos that followed the 2011 NATO-backed uprising that toppled longtime ruler Muammar Gaddafi. Two governments are currently vying for power: a UN-recognised administration in Tripoli led by Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah and its rival in the east backed by Haftar.
